slots.name: elected leaders courage
slots.sentence: When asked to select which category of people they most associated with courage, just 4 percent of Americans picked elected officials — tying with social media influencers, according to newly-published Gallup survey results.

slots.name: business athletes courage
slots.sentence: business leaders and athletes — which 2 percent of those polled associated with the trait.

slots.name: first responders courage
slots.sentence: The top responses included first responders at 60 percent, military personnel at 41 and nurses at 27.

slots.name: least courage elected
slots.sentence: More than half, 54 percent, picked elected officials as the category they saw as least tied to courage — the most common response to the question.

slots.name: military Republicans
slots.sentence: There were also party divides among respondents over which groups they viewed as most connected to the concept of courage, with 67 percent of Republicans choosing members of the military in their top three groups they see as most linked to the trait, while 37 percent of independents and 24 percent of Democrats did the same.

slots.name: leaders decision seen
slots.sentence: Despite not associating politicians with courage, the poll also found that 70 percent of respondents said they had “seen or heard about” American elected leaders standing “by a decision they believe is right even when they face personal attacks for it” within the last year.

slots.name: leaders disagreement seen
slots.sentence: Sixty-four percent of those polled also reported seeing or hearing about American elected leaders disagreeing “publicly with people on their own side, such as their political party, religious community or friends.”

slots.name: survey respondents
slots.sentence: The Gallup poll took place from May 12-22, featuring 3,199 respondents and a margin of error of 2.1 percentage points.

slots.name: poll group count
slots.sentence: In the new poll, released Wednesday, respondents were given a list of 16 different groups of people — such as first responders, scientists, teachers and the average American. Gallup then asked them to pick three they saw as most linked to courage — which Gallup defined as “deciding to do what’s right in the face of personal cost” — and three they associated with the word the least.
